text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Talks to finalise the long-awaited extradition treaty between Zimbabwe and South Africa have hit a snag, with Pretoria demanding that Harare undertakes not to administer capital punishment on all extradited prisoners, even in cases where such a sentence would be warranted under Zimbabwe law.

- The government and the Zimbabwe Investment Centre (ZIC) have threatened to cancel IBM Zimbabwe's licence to operate in the country after the American computer company failed to comply with national investment laws that require foreign firms to localise part of their equity.
- The government is actively scouting for black investors with money to acquire its equity in Bindura Nickel Corporation worth up to Z$280 million, official sources said in Harare this week.

- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has proposed that the Zimbabwe government double civil servants' pension contributions as well as cutting by half salaries of certain classes of its employees, but the government says the proposals are impractical.

- The European Union's financial support to Zimbabwe's export promotion body, Zimtrade's programmes is coming to an end with future aid hinging on the outcome of an evaluation exercise currently being carried out.

- What would have been an ordinary session of the Council of Ministers of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa in Lusaka, Zambia on Thursday is now expected to deal with a near-crisis following the withdrawal from the grouping of three countries amid allegations of mismanagement leveled against Comesa executive secretary Bingu wa Mutharika.

- Harare City Council's sluggish response to the ecological disaster at Manyame river appears to be in defiance of a High Court order last October for the council to stop any further discharge of sludge into the river.
